# Task P7-02: Release parsing — release-name quality and title, the `.torrent` reader, the NZB file list

**Phase:** 7 · **Depends on:** none · **Suggested tier:** cheap worker (T2) · **Estimated size:** M

## Goal
Indexers return releases (album-sized containers) described only by a name, a `.torrent` file or an NZB. This task gives Wondarr the pure, network-free readers it needs to judge them: the quality a release name claims, the artist/album/year a release name carries, the file list and info-hash inside a `.torrent`, and the file list inside an NZB. P7-04 (the container matcher) and P7-07 (grabbing) build on these. DECISIONS build session 8 #3, #4.

## Deliverables
All in `src/Wondarr.Sources.Torznab/Parsing/` (namespace `Wondarr.Sources.Torznab.Parsing`; the project exists and is referenced by the API and `tests/Wondarr.Sources.Tests`):

1. `ReleaseQualityParser.cs` — **ported from Lidarr** `src/NzbDrone.Core/Parser/QualityParser.cs` (the reference copy is `docs/build/tasks/ref/lidarr/Parser_QualityParser.cs.txt`): keep its codec, bitrate and sample-size regexes and decision structure, but return a Wondarr quality id from `src/Wondarr.Core/Domain/SeedData.cs`:
   - `public static long Parse(string releaseName)`; `1` (Unknown) when nothing is claimed.
   - FLAC → 36, FLAC with 24-bit (`24bit`, `24-bit`, `24 bit`, `24/96`, `[24-44]`, `TR24`, `Hi-Res`) → 40; ALAC → 37 / 41; APE → 38; WavPack → 39; WAV/PCM → 42; AIFF → 43.
   - MP3 CBR by bitrate: 320 → 29, 256 → 23, 224 → 18, 192 → 17, 160 → 14, 128 → 13, lower → the matching trash/poor id (5–12); `V0` → 30, `V2` → 24; an MP3 with no bitrate → 1 (Unknown — the probe decides after download).
   - AAC 320 → 31, 256 → 25, 192 → 19, AAC VBR → 32; Vorbis/Opus by Lidarr's rules mapped to the nearest seed row; WMA → 21.
   - Drop what does not apply (Lidarr's `QualityModel`, revision/version, the file-extension fallback that needs a path) and say so in a comment.
2. `ReleaseTitleParser.cs` — artist, album, year and the release-name's version hints from a release title, using the music part of Lidarr's `Parser.cs` (`docs/build/tasks/ref/lidarr/Parser_Parser.cs.txt`: the `ReportAlbumTitleRegex` family and its cleaning helpers). `public static ParsedRelease? Parse(string title)` → `record ParsedRelease(string Artist, string Album, int? Year, IReadOnlyList<string> Tags)` (tags such as `WEB`, `CD`, `Vinyl`, `Deluxe`, `Remastered`), or `null` when it cannot find an artist and album.
3. `TorrentMetainfo.cs` — our own bencode reader (not ported; DECISIONS #4). `public static TorrentMetainfo Parse(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data)` → `InfoHash` (40 lower-case hex chars: SHA-1 of the info dictionary's exact bytes as they appear in the file), `Name`, `Files` (`IReadOnlyList<TorrentFile>` with `Index` (0-based in file order), `Path` (`/`-joined, the torrent name as its first segment for a multi-file torrent; just the name for a single-file torrent), `Size`), `TotalSize`. Prefer `path.utf-8`/`name.utf-8` when present. A hybrid torrent (v1 `files` and v2 `file tree`) reads its v1 part; a v2-only torrent (`meta version` 2 and no `files`/`length`) throws `TorrentMetainfoException("v2-only torrents are not supported")`. Limits: input ≤ 10 MiB, nesting ≤ 64, a string length that runs past the end, a non-digit length, a missing `e`, or an integer with a leading zero → `TorrentMetainfoException` with the byte offset. Skip `.pad` files (BEP 47 `attr` containing `p`) from `Files` but keep `Index` numbering as the client numbers them (the client counts pad files; so `Index` is the position in the original list).
4. `NzbFileList.cs` — `public static IReadOnlyList<NzbFile> Parse(Stream nzb)` over the NZB XML (`http://www.newzbin.com/DTD/2003/nzb`; `XmlReaderSettings { DtdProcessing = Ignore, XmlResolver = null }`): per `<file>`, `Index` (order), `Subject`, `FileName` (the quoted name in the subject — `"name.flac"` — else the yEnc `name.ext yEnc` form, else `null`), `Size` (sum of `<segment bytes>`), `IsPar2` (`.par2`), `IsArchive` (`.rar`, `.r00`…, `.7z`, `.zip`, `.001`), `IsAudio` (flac, mp3, m4a, ogg, opus, wav, aiff, ape, wv), and `IsPlainName` (has a `FileName` that is not 16+ hex/base64-like characters before the extension). A helper `NzbFileList.IsClean(files)`: true when every file is audio, par2, or a small sidecar (`.nfo`, `.sfv`, `.jpg`, `.png`, `.cue`, `.log`, `.m3u`, `.txt`) with a plain name — DECISIONS #10.
5. Header comment on each ported file: `// Ported from Lidarr (https://github.com/Lidarr/Lidarr), src/NzbDrone.Core/Parser/QualityParser.cs at da7b4dfb1a9e7e1d6625c2dbc3fff96971ab26bd, GPL-3.0.` — and a row per ported file in `NOTICE.md` (the table format already there).

Tests in `tests/Wondarr.Sources.Tests/Torznab/Parsing/`:
- `ReleaseQualityParserTests` — a `[Theory]` of at least 40 real-world-style release names covering every mapping above (e.g. `Daft Punk - Discovery (2001) [FLAC 24bit-96kHz]` → 40, `Massive Attack-Mezzanine-CD-FLAC-1998-FATHEAD` → 36, `Artist - Album (2010) MP3 320` → 29, `Artist - Album [V0]` → 30, `Artist-Album-WEB-2019-MP3` → 1, `Artist - Album (2020) [AAC 256]` → 25).
- `ReleaseTitleParserTests` — at least 25 titles (scene style `Artist-Album-WEB-2019-GROUP`, `Artist - Album (Year) [Format]`, `Artist - Album {Deluxe Edition}`, Various Artists), and five that return `null`.
- `TorrentMetainfoTests` — bencode built in the test (a tiny `Bencode` writer in the test project): single-file, multi-file with nested paths, `path.utf-8` preferred, pad files skipped but indexes kept, the info-hash equals SHA-1 of the info bytes even when the outer dictionary has extra keys before and after `info`, hybrid read as v1, v2-only refused, and one test per malformed input above. Plus a fuzz-style test: 2 000 random byte mutations of a valid torrent never throw anything but `TorrentMetainfoException`.
- `NzbFileListTests` — fixtures `tests/fixtures/nzb/clean-album.nzb` (12 `.flac` files with quoted names + 2 `.par2`), `rar-album.nzb` (`.rar`/`.r00` set), `obfuscated.nzb` (hex names); subject forms; sizes summed; `IsClean` true/false/false; an NZB with a DOCTYPE does not resolve it.

## Constraints
- Pure functions, no I/O except reading the given stream; no new NuGet packages.
- Regexes compiled once (`static readonly` with `RegexOptions.Compiled | RegexOptions.IgnoreCase` and a match timeout of 1 s), as Lidarr does.
- Nullable enabled, warnings as errors, XML docs on public members.

## Acceptance criteria (each must be demonstrated)
1. `dotnet build -warnaserror` → `Build succeeded.`
2. `dotnet test tests/Wondarr.Sources.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Torznab.Parsing"` → all pass, with the counts above.
3. `python scripts/check-notice.py` → passes.
4. The examples named in the tests section give the stated results.
